summary: Backend-only testing of the rewritten Scheduling Engine. Wrote /app/backend/tests/test_scheduling_engine.py with 10 pytest cases covering every requested invariant. All 10 passed against the live public backend URL. Verified: (1) POST /api/tournaments/{tid}/auto-schedule returns {scheduled, unscheduled, conflicts, suggestions, categories} and GET /api/tournaments/{tid}/schedule populates date/time/ground_id on placed matches; (2) NO ground double-booking (checked overlap of [start, start+duration) on same (date, ground_id) across categories); (3) NO team overlap on same date; (4) min_rest_minutes respected between a team's back-to-back matches; (5) fixtures (home_id/away_id/round/order) are unchanged by scheduling; (6) locked match with date/time/ground is preserved across a re-run and other matches don't clash into it; (7) knockout progression — later rounds start after their feeders finish (Final >= max(SF end)); (8) infeasibility on a deliberately impossible single-day/6-team category returns 200 with unscheduled>0, a 'capacity' conflict, per-match 'unplaced_match' diagnostics and non-empty suggestions (no 500); (9) POST /api/categories/{cid}/auto-schedule returns the same-shape payload; (10) with 3 grounds and a 6-team league on one day, matches are distributed across grounds (>=2 grounds used, no single ground hosts >75%). Seeded tournaments (Verified League 6/6, CAWDADC 26+/1) both scheduled cleanly.
critical_code_review_comments: Pure `knockout` categories only schedule Round 1 in one pass because targets require home_id AND away_id, and later rounds are populated only when winners advance. This is by design but not obvious — consider documenting or allowing scheduling with unresolved teams (bracket slot placeholders) so the whole knockout can be placed up-front alongside groups.
server.py `update_match` accepts a raw Dict — a caller can set arbitrary fields (locked, status, etc.) with no validation. Consider a MatchUpdate Pydantic model.

scheduling.py `_score_slot`: `edges` derivation `sorted(set([lo] + ([brk[1]] if brk else []) + [e for (s,e) in blocks if e >= lo]))` can miss the natural step points `t += dur+gap` used by build_slots when the ground has no prior bookings — it currently only starts at `lo` and existing block-ends. That's fine for balance/parallelism today but if you want to expose non-contiguous slot alignment (e.g., always :00 / :30), it will need explicit stepping.

scheduling.py detects rest as `warning` in detect_conflicts but the engine enforces min_rest as hard. Divergence between hard-enforcement in scheduling and warning-only in reporting is minor but worth aligning severity to 'error' since the invariant is hard.

`_team_time_ok` treats `no_back_to_back` as `eff = max(min_rest, dur)`. A team that legitimately can play two 60-min matches with 60 min rest would still be blocked by NB2B (needing 60 min break, same as duration). Verify this matches product intent.
seed_data_creation: Test-owned tournaments created with TEST_ prefix for locked/knockout/infeasibility/balance cases; each cleaned up via DELETE /api/tournaments/{tid} in finally blocks. Seeded 'Verified League' and 'CAWDADC' tournaments were only read + auto-scheduled (no destructive edits).
